questions.stem: A notifier is written without braces: `if (optedIn)` / `    if (quietHours)` / `        queue(msg);` / `else` / `    askForConsent(user);`, with the `else` indented to the same column as `if (optedIn)`. It runs for a user who has opted in, outside quiet hours. What does it do?

options.text: It does not compile, since an else after two brace-less ifs could pair with either one
options.says: the grammar resolves it: the else binds to the nearest if without one, and the code compiles without a warning

options.text: It sends nothing, since the else pairs with the outer if, whose condition is true
options.says: javac ignores indentation; the else belongs to if (quietHours)

options.text: It asks for consent, since the else pairs with the inner if, whose condition is false
options.says: an else binds to the nearest if without one, here if (quietHours), whose condition is false

options.text: It does not compile, since an else after a nested brace-less if needs braces on the inner one
options.says: the inner if...else is one statement and the outer if owns it; javac accepts it

origin.section: An else Belongs to the Nearest if, Whatever the Indentation Says

questions.stem: A method declares `final String status;`, then `if (balance >= 0) { status = "ok"; } else if (balance < 0) { status = "overdrawn"; }`, and returns `status`. `balance` is an `int`. What does javac do?

options.text: It accepts the method, since flow analysis sees that the two conditions cover every int
options.says: javac doesn't evaluate what non-constant conditions mean; it reports that status might not have been initialized

options.text: It rejects the method, since flow analysis evaluates only conditions that are constants
options.says: definite assignment evaluates only constant expressions, so to javac there is a path where neither branch runs

options.text: It rejects the method, since flow analysis allows a final local only one assignment site
options.says: a blank final local may be assigned later, once on every path; a plain else makes this method compile

options.text: It accepts the method, since flow analysis gives an unassigned String local the value null
options.says: locals have no default value; reading one that might be unassigned is a compile error

origin.section: The Compiler Judges an if by Its Constants and Its Exits, Never by What Its Conditions Mean

questions.stem: An event handler starts with `if (!(event instanceof OrderPlaced placed)) { log.debug("skipping " + event); }` and its next line is `ship(placed.orderId());`. What happens?

options.text: It compiles, and for other events the call throws NullPointerException, since placed is left null
options.says: javac rejects the use with 'cannot find symbol'; the code never runs

options.text: It does not compile, since a pattern variable's scope ends with the if statement that declares it
options.says: a negated pattern whose if body returns or throws keeps the variable in scope after the if

options.text: It compiles, and for other events the call throws ClassCastException, since the cast happens at that use
options.says: javac rejects the use with 'cannot find symbol'; the code never runs

options.text: It does not compile, since the call can run for an event that is not an OrderPlaced
options.says: the binding is in scope after the if only when the if's body cannot complete normally; this body only logs

origin.section: The Compiler Judges an if by Its Constants and Its Exits, Never by What Its Conditions Mean

questions.stem: A class has `static final boolean AUDIT = false;`. One method wraps its audit logging in `if (AUDIT) { ... }`, and another wraps an audit loop in `while (AUDIT) { ... }`. What does javac do with them?

options.text: It compiles the if without its body and rejects the while, since the unreachable-code rule exempts if statements
options.says: JLS reachability exempts if so a constant flag can switch code off; while with a constant false condition is an unreachable statement

options.text: It compiles the while without its body and rejects the if, since the unreachable-code rule exempts loops
options.says: it is the other way round: if (AUDIT) compiles, while (AUDIT) is error: unreachable statement

options.text: It compiles both without their bodies, since a constant false condition is treated alike in both
options.says: while (AUDIT) with a constant false is error: unreachable statement

options.text: It compiles both with their bodies, since a static final field is read at run time like any field
options.says: a static final boolean initialised with a constant is a constant expression; javap shows the if body gone and the while is rejected

origin.section: The Compiler Judges an if by Its Constants and Its Exits, Never by What Its Conditions Mean
